text:
maria.g: heads up — at 14:05 we saw a large spike hitting eu-central1 realtime endpoints and the eu nodepool provisioning appears to be stalled. autoscaler logged timeouts and we still have queued requests. :warning:
jonathan.l: seeing same alerts. kubernetes events show provider quota errors and some image-pull timeouts. can anyone confirm if this is quota exhaustion or network egress throttling?
alek: quick paste from scale-controller logs:
```
2026-01-29T14:05:12Z scale-controller ERROR Provisioner timeout pool=eu-central1-gpu attempt=1
2026-01-29T14:05:15Z cloud-provision ERROR API 409 quotaExceeded: requested 8 gpus, available 0 in zone
2026-01-29T14:05:18Z kubelet WARN ImagePullBackOff registry.redwood-inference.internal: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
zara.k: hmm image pull errors could be a separate issue (registry cert). but quotaExceeded looks primary. infra-oncall-bot: alert created INFRA-4521 (severity=P2) — see https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4521
maria.g: attempted a manual nodepool create with different zone (eu-central1-b) but the cloud API returned quotaExceeded as well. fallback routing to us-west1 is partially blocked by our global egress policy (we limit cross-region burst).
jonathan.l: can we temporarily relax egress policy for the realtime LB to allow cross-region failover? that's the fastest mitigation if quota is regional.
alek: we can but need approval for temporary widening of egress. alternatively we can scale down non-critical batch deployments and free up GPUs. I've identified two big consumers: batch-encoder and nightly-eval; scaling them to 0.5x should free ~12 GPUs.
zara.k: doing that now — `kubectl scale deploy batch-encoder --replicas=1 -n ai-batches` and `kubectl scale deploy nightly-eval --replicas=0 -n evals`
infra-oncall-bot: action recorded by zara.k at 14:08
jonathan.l: I pushed a short-lived policy change to allow realtime LB to route to us-west1 for 20m (rollout id=rl-20260129-03). monitor only.
maria.g: after scaling batch jobs down we saw node provisioning succeed and two new gpu nodes joined the eu pool at 14:12. traffic recovered ~14:15 but we still observed elevated tail latency for 4 minutes while KV caches warmed.
alek: root causes we think: (1) momentary zone-level GPU quota exhaustion due to simultaneous batch start + sudden PLG surge, (2) registry cert flaps causing transient image pulls (worse during retries), and (3) strict cross-region egress gating slowed failover.
zara.k: immediate follow-ups: reopen quota request with cloud for eu-central1 GPUs, patch registry cert rotation to avoid short-lived cert windows, and add a warm-pool of 4 reserved GPUs for realtime (ticket INFRA-4522).
maria.g: cost note — warm-pool will add ~$6k/mo; we should discuss with finance if we want full-time reserved vs committed bursts.
jonathan.l: created a post-incident doc in /docs/incidents/INFRA-4521-eu-provision-stall.md and assigned owners. I'll also add an autoscaler change: add a 30s backoff override for image-pull retries so provisioning failures don't loop thrash.
infra-oncall-bot: incident marked resolved (P2) at 14:23, monitoring for 2h.
maria.g: thanks all — good job triaging. follow-ups in INFRA-4521 and INFRA-4522. :white_check_mark:
